Let $P$ be the point on the curve $y=\sqrt{x+1}$ that is closest to the origin (as shown above). Find the equation defining the $x$-coordinate of the point $P.$

$2x\,+$

{{field-1}}$=0$
question.worked_solution:
Let's consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(0,0)$ and a general point $P(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x,y) & =(x-0)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y=\sqrt{x+1}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x) & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+(\sqrt{x+1})^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(x)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(x)=2x+1 & =0 \\ 2x+1 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
